intro.can: Name the fingers and the seams, explain a simple grip adjustment in short Spanish instructions, and ask the pitcher what he feels.
intro.can_tr: Nombrar los dedos y las costuras, explicar un ajuste sencillo de agarre con instrucciones cortas en español y preguntarle al pícher qué siente.

outcomes.es: Nombrar los dedos, las partes de la mano y las costuras.
outcomes.en: Name the fingers, the parts of the hand and the seams.

outcomes.es: Decir dónde van los dedos: "Pon los dedos sobre las costuras."
outcomes.en: Say where the fingers go: "Pon los dedos sobre las costuras."

outcomes.es: Dar instrucciones cortas y suaves: separa, junta, mueve, afloja, aprieta… un poquito.
outcomes.en: Give short, soft instructions: spread, bring together, move, loosen, squeeze… a tiny bit.

outcomes.es: Elegir entre tú y usted, y usar las dos formas: pon / ponga.
outcomes.en: Choose between tú and usted, and use both forms: pon / ponga.

outcomes.es: Preguntar qué siente: "¿Cómo se siente ese agarre?"
outcomes.en: Ask what he feels: "¿Cómo se siente ese agarre?"

luis.name: Luis
luis.role: Pitcher, 19, from San Pedro de Macorís
luis.role_es: Pícher, 19 años, de San Pedro de Macorís

visual.title: Grips, fingers, and seams
visual.sub: Explaining a grip adjustment in Spanish

cues.text: In this lesson, you will learn to talk about grips in Spanish: the fingers, the seams, where the fingers go, and how much pressure to use.
You already know grips. The goal here is to explain one small adjustment clearly, and then ask the pitcher what he feels.
You will hear Coach Alex, a bilingual pitching coach, and Luis, a nineteen-year-old pitcher from the Dominican Republic. Repeat each Spanish line out loud when you hear it.

visual.title: The hand
visual.caption: Illustration: the fingers and parts of the hand.
visual.caption_es: Ilustración: los dedos y las partes de la mano.

cues.text: Start with the hand. Spanish names every finger, so you can be exact.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el dedo índice

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el dedo medio… el dedo del medio
cues.en: the middle finger (both forms are common)

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el pulgar

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el anular y el meñique
cues.en: the ring finger and the pinky

cues.text: Then the parts of the hand you will mention most in grip work.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la palma, la muñeca, las yemas de los dedos
cues.en: the palm, the wrist, the fingertip pads

cues.text: On the field, many players simply say the tips of the fingers.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la punta de los dedos

visual.title: The ball and the seams
visual.caption: Illustration: the seams and the horseshoe.
visual.caption_es: Ilustración: las costuras y la herradura.

cues.text: Now the ball itself.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la pelota
You will also hear this word. It also means a ball in the count, so for the object in his hand, the first word is clearer.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la bola
cues.en: the ball; also a ball in the count

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: las costuras

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la herradura
The horseshoe is the U-shaped part of the seams. It gives you a quick way to name the seam you mean.

visual.title: Four-seam fastball
visual.caption: Illustration: one common four-seam grip. Grips are individual.
visual.caption_es: Ilustración: un agarre común de cuatro costuras. Cada agarre es individual.

cues.text: Here is a four-seam grip. The pitch is called…

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la recta de cuatro costuras
And the grip itself is…

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el agarre
Listen to Coach Alex describe where the fingers go.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Pon los dedos sobre las costuras.
cues.en: Put your fingers on the seams.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: El índice y el medio, encima de la herradura.
cues.en: Index and middle finger on top of the horseshoe.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: El pulgar, debajo de la pelota.
Notice that Spanish says the fingers, not your fingers. With parts of the body, that is normal, and it does not sound cold.

visual.title: Two-seam and sinker
visual.caption: Illustration: one common two-seam grip. Grips are individual.
visual.caption_es: Ilustración: un agarre común de dos costuras. Cada agarre es individual.

cues.text: Pitch names mix Spanish and English. That is normal in Dominican baseball, and in Spanish-language baseball media.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la recta de dos costuras

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el sinker, el slider, el cutter
cues.en: the sinker, the slider, the cutter

cues.text: These English names are usually masculine. You may hear the feminine too, and either will be understood. Some pitches also have a Spanish name.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la recta cortada… la curva
And for the session itself, the English word stays.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la sesión de bullpen

visual.title: Short instructions

rows.example: Pon los dedos sobre las costuras.
rows.en: Put your fingers on the seams.
Move your thumb a tiny bit.

visual.note_en: A verb, then the finger or the grip. "Un poco" (a little) and "un poquito" (a tiny bit) make a correction sound like a small adjustment, not a criticism.

cues.text: Between pitches, short instructions are normal. Start with the verb, then the finger or the grip.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Separa un poco los dedos.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Junta los dedos.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Mueve el pulgar un poquito.
cues.en: Move your thumb a tiny bit.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Afloja un poco el agarre.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Aprieta un poco más.
Listen to the small words at the end: a little, a tiny bit. They soften the instruction. It sounds like an adjustment you are trying together, not a mistake he made.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: un poco… un poquito

visual.title: Two ways to say "you"
visual.note_en: First form: tú (informal), normal with young academy players. Second form: usted (formal), for older or veteran players, staff and parents, or when you're unsure. This is working guidance, not a fixed rule; when in doubt, ask.

cues.text: Spanish has two ways to say you. The informal one is normal with young academy players.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: tú

The formal one is for older or veteran players, staff and parents, or when you are not sure. That is guidance, not a fixed rule. Players may address you formally even when you speak informally to them.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: usted
In instructions, the formal form usually changes the last vowel. Listen to each pair.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Pon… ponga.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Mueve… mueva.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Separa… separe.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Prueba… pruebe.
If you are unsure which one a player prefers, ask him. It is a respectful question.

visual.title: Changeup: depth and pressure
visual.caption: Illustration: one common changeup grip. Grips are individual.
visual.caption_es: Ilustración: un agarre común de cambio. Cada agarre es individual.

cues.text: The changeup has two names. Both are standard.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: el cambio… el cambio de velocidad
Pressure is part of the grip too.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: la presión
And depth: is the ball deep in the hand, or out in the fingertips?

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: más adentro en la mano… en la punta de los dedos
cues.en: deeper in your hand… out in your fingertips

cues.text: Finally, the moment the ball leaves the hand.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: soltar la pelota

visual.title: Listen to Coach Alex and Luis
visual.title_es: Escucha al coach Alex y a Luis

cues.text: Now listen to Coach Alex with Luis during a bullpen. Alex suggests one change, then asks how it feels.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Luis, separa un poco los dedos. Así.
cues.en: Luis, spread your fingers a little. Like this.

cues.speaker: luis
cues.text: ¿Así, coach?

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: Eso. ¿Cómo se siente ese agarre?
cues.en: That's it. How does that grip feel?

cues.speaker: luis
cues.text: Cómodo. Un poco raro, pero cómodo.
cues.en: Comfortable. A little strange, but comfortable.

cues.text: After the pitch, ask about the release.

cues.speaker: alex
cues.text: ¿Qué sentiste cuando soltaste la pelota?
cues.en: What did you feel when you let go of the ball?

cues.speaker: luis
cues.text: La sentí mejor en los dedos.
cues.en: It felt better in my fingers.

cues.text: One change, then a question. His answer tells you whether to keep the adjustment or try something else. Next, you will practise these words, build sentences, and then coach Luis through a grip change yourself.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Luis, vamos a empezar con la recta de cuatro costuras.
lines.en: Luis, let's start with the four-seam fastball.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Ok, coach. ¿Cómo pongo los dedos?
lines.en: OK, Coach. How do I put my fingers?

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: El índice y el medio sobre la herradura. El pulgar, debajo de la pelota.
lines.en: Index and middle finger on the horseshoe. Thumb under the ball.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: ¿Así?
lines.en: Like this?

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Eso. Ahora separa un poquito los dedos y tira cinco rectas.
lines.en: That's it. Now spread your fingers a tiny bit and throw five fastballs.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Coach, el cambio se me queda arriba.
lines.en: Coach, my changeup keeps staying up.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: ¿Cómo lo estás agarrando?
lines.en: How are you gripping it?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Bien fuerte, en la punta de los dedos.
lines.en: Really tight, out in my fingertips.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Vamos a probar algo. Ponla más adentro en la mano y afloja un poco el agarre.
lines.en: Let's try something. Set it deeper in your hand and loosen your grip a little.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: ¿Más adentro? Ok.
lines.en: Deeper? OK.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Tira tres. Después me dices cómo se siente.
lines.en: Throw three. Then tell me how it feels.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Pon los dedos sobre las costuras. Separa un poco los dedos.
lines.en: Put your fingers on the seams. Spread them a little.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: ¿Cómo se siente ese agarre? ¿Qué sentiste cuando soltaste la pelota?
lines.en: How does that grip feel? What did you feel when you let go of the ball?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Coach, ¿dónde pongo el pulgar?
lines.en: Coach, where do I put my thumb?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Coach, este agarre lo siento muy apretado.
lines.en: Coach, this grip feels really tight.

lines.speaker: alex
lines.text: Afloja un poco el agarre.
lines.en: Loosen your grip a little.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Coach, ¿cómo quieres que agarre la pelota?
lines.en: Coach, how do you want me to grip the ball?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Ok, así. Entendido.
lines.en: OK, like this. Got it.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Perdón, coach, no te entendí. ¿Dónde pongo los dedos?
lines.en: Sorry, Coach, I didn't understand. Where do I put my fingers?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Siento los dedos muy juntos. ¿Los dejo así?
lines.en: My fingers feel very close together. Should I leave them like this?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Ok, un poquito más separados.
lines.en: OK, a little further apart.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: ¿Cómo, coach? ¿Los separo o los junto?
lines.en: Sorry, Coach? Should I spread them or bring them together?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: ¿Y el pulgar? Lo tengo al lado de la pelota.
lines.en: And my thumb? I have it on the side of the ball.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Ok. Voy a tirar una.
lines.en: OK. I'm going to throw one.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Perdón, ¿dónde va el pulgar?
lines.en: Sorry, where does the thumb go?

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Listo, coach. Ya tiré con el agarre nuevo.
lines.en: Done, Coach. I threw it with the new grip.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Se siente cómodo. La pelota salió mejor de los dedos.
lines.en: It feels comfortable. The ball came off my fingers better.

lines.speaker: luis
lines.text: Perdón, coach, ¿qué me preguntaste?
lines.en: Sorry, Coach, what did you ask me?

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish word with its meaning.
activities.explain_en: "Dedo medio" and "dedo del medio" both mean the middle finger; the second is the everyday form. "Soltar" means to let go: "cuando soltaste la pelota" = when you let go of the ball.

figure.caption: Numbers show each finger; tap Expand for a larger view.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish word with its meaning.
activities.explain_en: "La herradura" is the U-shaped part of the seams. "La recta" is the everyday word for the fastball; "la recta de cuatro costuras" is the four-seamer.

activities.intro: Coach Alex starts a bullpen with Luis. Listen and answer.

questions.prompt: Which pitch are they starting with?
questions.explain: "Vamos a empezar con la recta de cuatro costuras": let's start with the four-seam fastball.

questions.prompt: Where do the index and middle fingers go?
questions.explain: "El índice y el medio sobre la herradura": index and middle finger on the horseshoe. The thumb goes under the ball.

questions.prompt: What does Alex ask Luis to do at the end?
options: Spread his fingers a tiny bit and throw five fastballs
Bring his fingers together and throw three changeups
questions.explain: "Separa un poquito los dedos y tira cinco rectas": spread your fingers a tiny bit and throw five fastballs.

activities.intro: Luis has a problem with his changeup. Listen and answer.

questions.prompt: What is the problem with Luis's changeup?
questions.explain: "El cambio se me queda arriba": my changeup keeps staying up.

questions.prompt: Which two changes does Alex suggest?
options: Set the ball deeper in the hand and loosen the grip
Move the thumb and squeeze harder
Spread the fingers and throw harder
questions.explain: "Ponla más adentro en la mano y afloja un poco el agarre": set it deeper in your hand and loosen your grip a little.

questions.prompt: What does Alex want after three pitches?
options: Luis to tell him how it feels
Luis to go back to the fastball
questions.explain: "Después me dices cómo se siente": then tell me how it feels. He tests the change and asks about the feel.

activities.explain: "Las costuras" are the seams. "Las yemas" are the fingertip pads; "la muñeca" is the wrist.

activities.prompt: You're talking to a 17-year-old academy pitcher. Which instruction sounds most natural?
activities.explain: With a young academy player, the informal "mueve" is normal. The infinitive "mover" sounds like a written manual, and "señor" is far too formal here.

activities.prompt: You've just met a veteran pitcher in his thirties. Which instruction is the safer choice?
options: Ponga los dedos sobre las costuras.
Poner los dedos sobre las costuras.
Pones los dedos sobre las costuras.
activities.explain: "Ponga" is the formal (usted) instruction: a respectful default with an older player until you know what he prefers. This is guidance, not a rule; you can also simply ask.

activities.prompt: Build the sentence: "Spread your fingers a little."
activities.explain_en: Verb first: "Separa", then "un poco" and "los dedos". Spanish says "los dedos" (the fingers), not "tus dedos".

figure.caption: "Separa un poco los dedos" — a small change in spacing.

activities.prompt: Luis is squeezing his changeup very tight. Which instruction fits?
activities.explain: "Afloja" means loosen. "Aprieta" means squeeze, the opposite. "Junta los dedos" (bring your fingers together) doesn't address pressure.

figure.caption: A changeup sits deeper; pressure can ease off.

activities.prompt: Build the question: "How does that grip feel?"
activities.explain_en: "¿Cómo se siente…?" = How does … feel? Written Spanish opens a question with ¿ and closes it with ?.

activities.prompt: Which question asks about the release?
activities.explain: "Soltaste la pelota" = you let go of the ball. The other two mean "Where do I put my thumb?" and "How many pitches are left?"

activities.prompt: Why does a coach say "Pon los dedos…" and not "Pon tus dedos…"?
options: With body parts, Spanish normally uses "the". It isn't cold.
"Tus" is rude in the Dominican Republic.
"Los dedos" only means the index and middle fingers.
activities.explain: In Spanish, it's clear whose fingers they are, so the article "los" (the) is normal: "Mueve el pulgar", "Separa los dedos".

activities.prompt: Build the sentence: "Put your fingers on the seams."
activities.en: Put your fingers on the seams.
answers: pon los dedos sobre las costuras
activities.explain_en: "Pon" (put) + "los dedos" (your fingers) + "sobre las costuras" (on the seams).

activities.prompt: Which instruction sounds like a small adjustment, not a criticism?
options: Siempre tienes que mover el pulgar.
activities.explain: "Un poquito" (a tiny bit) frames it as a small change to try. "Ese pulgar está mal" (that thumb is wrong) blames, and "siempre tienes que" (you always have to) turns one adjustment into a rule.

activities.text: Pon los dedos sobre las costuras. Separa un poco los dedos.
activities.en: Put your fingers on the seams. Spread them a little.
activities.tip_en: Spanish vowels are short and clear: "cos-TU-ras", "SE-pa-ra". Stress the verb at the start.

figure.caption: Index and middle fingers across the seams.

activities.text: ¿Cómo se siente ese agarre? ¿Qué sentiste cuando soltaste la pelota?
activities.en: How does that grip feel? What did you feel when you let go of the ball?
activities.tip_en: Let your voice rise slightly at the end of each question. "Sentiste" and "soltaste" are both stressed on the middle syllable.

activities.prompt_en: Coach, where do I put my thumb?
activities.goal: The learner tells the pitcher, in Spanish, where to put his thumb (e.g. under the ball / debajo de la pelota, or move it a little / mueve el pulgar un poquito). Any clear, reasonable placement counts; a short informal (tú) instruction is expected, and adding a check such as "prueba así" or "¿cómo se siente?" is a plus. Do not require one exact sentence.
activities.goal_en: Tell Luis where to put his thumb, in a short instruction.
examples: Ponlo debajo de la pelota. Prueba así.
Mueve el pulgar un poquito, debajo de la pelota. ¿Cómo se siente?
El pulgar, debajo de la pelota. Así.

figure.caption: "Mueve el pulgar un poquito": where the thumb goes.

activities.prompt: Coach, este agarre lo siento muy apretado.
activities.prompt_en: Coach, this grip feels really tight.
activities.goal: The learner responds to a grip that feels too tight: suggests loosening it a little (afloja / agárrala más suave / no aprietes tanto), ideally softened with "un poco" or "un poquito", and asks how it feels or invites him to try one. Communication matters more than exact wording.
activities.goal_en: Suggest loosening the grip a little, then ask how it feels.
examples: Afloja un poco el agarre. ¿Cómo se siente ahora?
Ok, agárrala más suave. Prueba así.
No aprietes tanto. Afloja un poquito y tira otra.

activities.setting: Bullpen session at the academy. Luis, 19, is holding the ball before a set of four-seam fastballs and asks you about his grip. Speak Spanish and use tú with him.
activities.objective: Explain how to place and move his fingers, name the seam, and ask whether the new grip feels comfortable.

turns.line: Coach, ¿cómo quieres que agarre la pelota?
turns.en: Coach, how do you want me to grip the ball?
turns.goal: Tell the pitcher where to put his fingers, naming the seams or the horseshoe (e.g. on/over the seams, index and middle on the horseshoe). Any clear placement counts.
turns.goal_en: Tell Luis where his fingers go, and name the seam.
examples: Pon los dedos sobre las costuras.
El índice y el medio encima de la herradura.

options: Pon el índice y el medio sobre la herradura.
La pelota está en el bullpen.

clarify.line: Perdón, coach, no te entendí. ¿Dónde pongo los dedos?
clarify.en: Sorry, Coach, I didn't understand. Where do I put my fingers?

turns.line: Siento los dedos muy juntos. ¿Los dejo así?
turns.en: My fingers feel very close together. Should I leave them like this?
turns.goal: Give one adjustment to the finger spacing (e.g. spread them a little: separa un poco los dedos), ideally softened with un poco / un poquito. Suggesting he try it and see how it feels is also fine.
turns.goal_en: Suggest one small change to the spacing of his fingers.
examples: No, sepáralos un poco. Prueba así.

clarify.en: Sorry, Coach? Should I spread them or bring them together?

turns.line: ¿Y el pulgar? Lo tengo al lado de la pelota.
turns.en: And my thumb? I have it on the side of the ball.
turns.goal: Tell him where to put or move his thumb (e.g. under the ball, move it a little underneath). Any clear, reasonable placement counts.
turns.goal_en: Tell Luis where to move his thumb.
examples: Mueve el pulgar un poquito, debajo de la pelota.
Ponlo debajo de la pelota. Prueba así.

options: Mueve el pulgar un poquito, debajo de la pelota.
El pulgar es el dedo índice.

ack.en: OK. I'm going to throw one.

clarify.en: Sorry, where does the thumb go?

turns.line: Listo, coach. Ya tiré con el agarre nuevo.
turns.en: Done, Coach. I threw it with the new grip.
turns.goal: Ask whether the new grip feels comfortable or natural, and/or what he felt when he released the ball (e.g. ¿Cómo se siente ese agarre? ¿Te sientes cómodo? ¿Qué sentiste cuando soltaste la pelota?).
turns.goal_en: Ask Luis whether the new grip feels comfortable.

options: Tienes que usar este agarre siempre.

ack.line: Se siente cómodo. La pelota salió mejor de los dedos.
ack.en: It feels comfortable. The ball came off my fingers better.

clarify.en: Sorry, Coach, what did you ask me?

figure.caption: The two adjustments you will talk Luis through.

options: the U-shaped part of the seams
the tip of the index finger
items.explain: "La herradura" (the horseshoe) is the U-shaped seam pattern.

items.prompt: Which is the formal (usted) form of "Prueba así"?
items.explain: Informal "prueba" becomes formal "pruebe": the last vowel changes, as in pon / ponga and mueve / mueva.

items.prompt: You want Luis to spread his fingers a little. You say:

options: Do you want a new grip?
items.explain: "¿Cómo se siente…?" = How does … feel? Ask it after every change.

items.prompt: Listen. What does Coach Alex say?
options: Squeeze the ball a little more.
items.explain: "Afloja un poco el agarre": loosen your grip a little.

phrases.es: Pon los dedos sobre las costuras.
phrases.en: Put your fingers on the seams.

phrases.es: El índice y el medio, encima de la herradura.
phrases.en: Index and middle finger on top of the horseshoe.

phrases.es: El pulgar, debajo de la pelota.
phrases.note: "El dedo gordo" is a common colloquial name for the thumb in the Caribbean; "pulgar" is understood everywhere.

phrases.es: Separa un poco los dedos. / Junta los dedos.
phrases.en: Spread your fingers a little. / Bring your fingers together.
Move your thumb a tiny bit.
phrases.note: Usted: "Mueva el pulgar…". "Un poquito" softens any instruction.

phrases.es: Afloja un poco el agarre. / Aprieta un poco más.
phrases.en: Loosen your grip a little. / Squeeze a little more.
phrases.note: Usted: afloje / apriete. Field alternative: "Agárrala más suave."

phrases.es: Ponla más adentro en la mano.
phrases.en: Set the ball deeper in your hand.

phrases.es: En la punta de los dedos.
phrases.note: Field form. "Las yemas de los dedos" is more precise and a little more formal.

phrases.en: What did you feel when you let go of the ball?
phrases.note: Say "¿Cómo te sentiste?" or "¿Qué sentiste?" — not "¿Cómo sentiste?" on its own.

phrases.en: Are you comfortable? / Does it feel natural?

phrases.es: la recta de cuatro costuras / el sinker de dos costuras
phrases.en: the four-seam fastball / the two-seam sinker
phrases.note: Loanwords (sinker, slider, cutter, bullpen) are normal baseball Spanish and usually masculine; you may also hear "la sinker".
Both forms are standard; "el cambio" is the everyday one.

next: Next: Lesson 2, delivery and mechanics — describing what you saw on a pitch, asking what he felt, and suggesting one adjustment to test. Before that, review the phrases you missed and say the grip instructions out loud.
